question: Can three ORT Web sessions coexist in one WebAssembly heap, and does teardown reclaim?
scope: Lifecycle mechanics with ONE 174-byte two-op model. Does NOT exercise the ~120 MB resident-model case the dossier's risk is actually about.
measurement_rule: A WebAssembly.Memory cannot shrink - the specification provides grow() and no inverse. The heap staying put after teardown is CORRECT behaviour and is not a leak. The leak question lives in repeated create/infer/destroy cycles.

wasm_heap_instrumentation.method: WebAssembly.Memory is wrapped before ORT loads; every constructed instance is retained and its buffer.byteLength summed.
wasm_heap_instrumentation.why: performance.memory is Chrome-only, JS-only, absent in workers, and GC-timing-dominated. This experiment contains its own proof of that: one cell shows the JS heap dropping 25.9 -> 10.8 MB in a single step.

runtime.generated_or_transformed: No. Copied byte-for-byte from the pinned npm package by harness/build-extension.js.
runtime.fetched_at_runtime: No. ort.env.wasm.wasmPaths points at the extension's own packaged files. No network fetch for runtime or model.
runtime.committed: No. CI blocks files over 5 MB and SECURITY.md requires large binaries be referenced by pinned revision.

model.graph: Mul by 2 then Add 1 over float32[1, 262144]; opset 13, ir_version 9
model.why_not_committed: verify-repo.py bans .onnx and that rule is correct. Reproducible from the committed build_model.py and pinned by the sha256 above.
model.provenance: generated synthetic. NOT a production model. No Qwen. Nothing downloaded.

csp.status: THROWAWAY HARNESS ONLY. Required because both Chrome MV3 and Firefox MV3 block WebAssembly without it (S-02a-2, S-02a-2b), and wasm-unsafe-eval is the only token Chrome MV3 accepts (S-02a-2b-1). NOT adopted. There is no product code. The decision remains ADR S-02a-2a.
csp.multi_session_security_delta: None found. Session count does not change the trust boundary: same packaged bytes, same origin, same CSP requirement, no additional network access, no new executable input.

windows.host: HP OMEN 16-ap0xxx, Windows 11 10.0.26200, AMD Ryzen AI 7 350, RTX 5050 + Radeon 860M

linux-wsl2.gpu: no /dev/dri, 0 Vulkan ICDs, llvmpipe. WebGPU failures here are ENVIRONMENTAL.

cycles: 5 create-3/infer/destroy-3 cycles per cell (3 cycles in the threading run)
threading_run: numThreads 1 vs 4, Chrome only, where SharedArrayBuffer is available

data.verification: element-by-element against a CPU reference on EVERY inference
